image_description: A close-up, high-resolution portrait of a male Mallard duck (drake) in profile facing right. The image highlights the iridescent emerald green head, a distinct white neck ring, a bright yellow bill with a black tip and nostril, and dark brown/grey chest plumage. The background is a soft, out-of-focus bokeh of earthy tones.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, exhibiting the characteristic broad, flat shape and vibrant yellow coloration with a black tip, consistent with a Mallard drake.
The eye is visible as a small, dark, circular feature on the side of the head, matching the biological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although only the upper torso is visible, the plumage appears dense and tightly packed with realistic texture, suggesting a waterproof, streamlined body structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image perfectly matches the Mallard pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and darker chest/body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The framing is a tight head-and-shoulders shot; the legs and feet are completely outside the field of view and cannot be evaluated.
The wings are largely occluded by the angle and framing; only the shoulder area is visible, making it impossible to verify the full shape of the wings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is located at the rear of the animal and is entirely outside the frame of this close-up portrait.
